contradictions.what: Earlier steps treated the Cochetopa designation as untouched by later held instruments. Held EO 6881 and EO 8030 modify the forest boundary (transfers between Cochetopa and Gunnison/Rio Grande), and the BLM PLO table lists PLO 258 (Jan. 17, 1945) transferring lands from Cochetopa NF to Gunnison, Rio Grande and San Isabel NFs (possible dissolution; the held entry does not say 'abolishing'). The Cochetopa NF is thus not shown current at 2026-10-14 on held evidence; the designation was at least partly overtaken by later orders. Positive for the rename: later orders use the name Cochetopa National Forest.

contradictions.what: Earlier steps said no held source shows the Cabinet NF designation later changed. The BLM PLO table lists PLO 965 (May 19, 1954) abolishing Cabinet National Forest and transferring its lands to Kootenai, Kaniksu and Lolo NFs. On held evidence the designation made by EO 838 ended 1954-05-19 (index entry only; PLO text itself not held), so it is not current at 2026-10-14. Earlier modifications (EO 3043 excluding land; EO 5758 adding Lolo lands) are boundary changes, not ends.
